source.title: Open Problems on Connectivity of Fibers with Positive Margins in Multi-dimensional Contingency Tables

accepted.question_text: Let A_T be the design matrix of a statistical model for contingency tables, let F_T = {n in N^k : A_T(n) = A_T(n_obs)} be the fiber of the observed table n_obs, let M be a lattice basis in ker(A_T), let p = x_1 ··· x_k, and for each index ℓ with t_ℓ > 0, where t = A_T(n_obs), let I_ℓ = <x_h>_{A_T(ℓ,h)>0} be the monomial ideal generated by the indeterminates corresponding to cells that contribute to margin ℓ. If L is the collection of indices ℓ with t_ℓ > 0 and I_L = (I_M : ∏_{ℓ∈L} I_ℓ), does the condition (I_L : (I_L : p)) = <1> already imply that the moves in M connect all tables in the fiber F_T even without assuming that the toric ideal I_M is radical?
accepted.context_brief: Radical-free connectivity criterion for positive margins

evidence.quote: Conjecture 1. Suppose M is a lattice basis. Let p = x1 · · · xk, let t = AT (nobs), and let tℓ be the ℓ-th coordinate of t. For each index ℓ with tℓ > 0, let Iℓ = ⟨xh⟩AT (ℓ,h)>0 be the monomial ideal generated by indeterminates for cells that contribute to margin ℓ. Let L be the collection of indices ℓ with tℓ > 0. Define IL as in Theorem 2. If the equation in (6) satisfies, then the moves in M connect all the tables in FT .

accepted.question_text: Assume all margins of the contingency tables are positive, so that rows or columns with zero marginals are excluded as necessary zeros. Find an algorithm that computes, with respect to set inclusion, a minimum set of Markov moves connecting all tables in the fiber F_T = {n in N^k : A_T(n) = A_T(n_obs)}.
accepted.context_brief: Minimal connecting moves under positive margins

evidence.quote: Problem 1. Assume that all margins are positive. Find an algorithm to compute a min￾imum set of moves connecting all tables in FT in terms of inclusions.

accepted.question_text: Let t = A_T(n_obs) be the margin vector for a contingency-table model, and suppose t_ℓ > 0 for at least one row index ℓ. Find an algorithm that computes, in terms of set inclusion, a minimum set of moves M that connects all tables in the fiber F_T = {n in N^k : A_T(n) = A_T(n_obs)}.
accepted.context_brief: Minimal connecting set with partially positive margins

evidence.quote: Problem 2. With tℓ > 0 for some row index ℓ, find an algorithm to compute a minimum set of moves M in terms of inclusion connecting all tables in FT .

accepted.question_text: Let t = A_T(n_obs) be the margin vector for a contingency-table model, suppose t_ℓ > 0 for some row index ℓ, and let F_T = {n in N^k : A_T(n) = A_T(n_obs)}. Develop an algorithm that computes, in terms of set inclusion, a minimum set of moves M connecting all tables in F_T and that is faster than computing a full Markov basis via geometry-based algorithms such as those implemented in 4ti2.

evidence.quote: Problem 3. With tℓ > 0 for some row index ℓ, develop an algorithm to compute a minimum set of moves M in terms of inclusion which connects all tables in FT faster than computing a full Markov basis via algorithms using geometry such as implemented in 4ti2.

accepted.question_text: Let X = {1, ..., I} × {1, ..., J} be the cell set of an I × J contingency table with fixed row and column sums, let S ⊂ X be the set of structural-zero cells, and assume the margins are positive. A basic move is the square-free degree-two move on a 2 × 2 subtable with +1 at (i,j) and (i',j') and −1 at (i,j') and (i',j) for i ≠ i' and j ≠ j'. What is the necessary and sufficient condition on S for the set of basic moves to form a Markov subbasis for the contingency tables with structural zeros in S under the assumption of positive marginals?

evidence.quote: Problem 4. Let S ⊂ X be the set of structural zeros. Suppose we have I × J tables with fixed row and column sums. What is the necessary and sufficient condition on S so that a set of basic moves is a Markov subbasis for I × J contingency tables with structural zeros in S under the assumption of positive marginals.
For i ̸= i′ and j ̸= j′, consider the square￾free move of degree two with +1 at cells (i, j), (i′, j′) and −1 at cells (i, j′) and (i′, j) ... For simplicity we call this a basic move.

accepted.question_text: Consider logistic regression with m covariates. For a level combination j = (j_1, ..., j_m), let e_j be the array with 1 at cell (1, j) and −1 at cell (2, j). Define B_{Λ(A_1⊗···⊗A_m)} to be the set of moves m of the form m = e_{j_1} − e_{j_2} − e_{j_3} + e_{j_4} such that j_1 − j_2 = j_3 − j_4. Does this set of moves connect every fiber whose response marginals are all positive for the logistic regression model with m covariates?
accepted.context_brief: Positive-marginal connectivity for m-covariate logistic regression

evidence.quote: Then we have the following conjecture. Conjecture 2. The set of moves BΛ(A1⊗···⊗Am) connects every fiber with positive response marginals for the logistic regression with m covariates.

Theorem 5 shows the connectivity result for fibers with positive response variable marginals for bivariate logistic regression. There is a natural extension of Theorem 5 to m covariates: Let j = (j1, . . . , jm) denote the combination of m levels and let ej denote an array with 1 at the cell (1, j) and −1 at the cell (2, j). Define BΛ(A1⊗···⊗Am) as the set of the following moves m: 1. m = ej1 − ej2 − ej3 + ej4 2. j1 − j2 = j3 − j4 .

accepted.question_text: In the same m-covariate logistic-regression setting, consider only those moves in B_{Λ(A_1⊗···⊗A_m)} for which every coordinate of the difference vectors j_1 − j_2 = j_3 − j_4 is in {−1, 0, 1}. Does this restricted subset already connect every fiber with positive response marginals for the logistic regression with m covariates?
accepted.context_brief: Restricted local-move connectivity for m-covariate logistic regression

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3. The subset of moves from BΛ(A1⊗···⊗Am) such that the elements of j1−j2 = j3 − j4 are ±1 or 0 connects every fiber with positive response marginals for the logistic regression with m covariates.

needs_review.question_text_raw: Thus it would be interesting to investigate the cases if we have that the coefficient of one of the covariates is zero in the bivariate logistic regression.
